text: The bogan is a Scottish folkloric figure, occasionally Irish. It is also called buckawn, bocan, or bauchan. This shape-shifting night sprite was a trickster. It helped sometimes but was usually malicious. It appears often in the Highlands, less in Ireland. It also reached America with those it served or haunted. The MacDonald clan of Morar kept a bogan called Coluinn gun Cheann. He was cheerful to the family. He tended to murder visitors and leave mutilated bodies by the river. Finally he killed a man. The victim's strong friend John Macleod took revenge. Macleod wrestled the bogan down and threatened daylight. The bogan promised to leave the land if freed. It kept its promise.
